name: putnam_1988_a5
story: THE RUNAWAY FEEDBACK LOOP. Any nonzero error is amplified by (9/4) each step and escapes every bound — so the error must be exactly zero.
statement: theorem putnam_1988_a5 : (∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ x > 0, f (f x) = 6 * x - f x ∧ f x > 0) ∧ (∀ g : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ x > 0, g (g x) = 6 * x - g x ∧ g x > 0) → (∀ x > 0, f x = g x))) :=

story: PINNED TO THE RIM. Not inside the circle, not outside it — so every root lies exactly ON it. Trichotomy does the work.

name: putnam_1991_b4
story: BELOW THE NOISE FLOOR. Working mod p², anything carrying p² is dust: drop it. Cross terms vanish and a hard binomial identity goes linear.
statement: theorem putnam_1991_b4 (p : ℕ) (podd : Odd p) (pprime : Prime p) : (∑ j : Fin (p + 1), (p.choose j) * ((p + j).choose j)) ≡ (2 ^ p + 1) [MOD (p ^ 2)] :=

name: putnam_1993_a2
story: A CONSERVED QUANTITY. Like energy: a ratio built from the sequence never changes. Measure it once at the start; it pins every later term.
statement: theorem putnam_1993_a2 (x : ℕ → ℝ) (xnonzero : ∀ n : ℕ, x n ≠ 0) (hx : ∀ n ≥ 1, (x n) ^ 2 - x (n - 1) * x (n + 1) = 1) : ∃ a : ℝ, ∀ n ≥ 1, x (n + 1) = a * x n - x (n - 1) :=

name: putnam_1996_a5
story: PAIR OFF THE DANCERS, ON THE MIDDLE THIRD. p | C(p,i) lets you divide the whole problem by p, dropping it into the FIELD ZMod p. What is left is a harmonic sum over (p/3, 2p/3] — a range symmetric under i ↦ p-i, where 1/(p-i) = -1/i. The sum is its own negative: it is 0.
statement: theorem putnam_1996_a5 (p : ℕ) (hpprime : Prime p) (hpge3 : p > 3) (k : ℕ) (hk : k = Nat.floor (2*p/(3 : ℚ))) : p^2 ∣ ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, Nat.choose p i :=

name: putnam_1997_b5
story: THE TOWER STOPS MATTERING. Above a certain height a power tower is invisible mod n — like a clock, only the remainder shows. Recurse on the MODULUS (Euler/totient), not on the tower.
statement: theorem putnam_1997_b5 (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≥ 2) : tetration 2 n ≡ tetration 2 (n-1) [MOD n] :=
